# dsh-prompt-optimizer
A standalone, independently distributed plugin family for the DeepSeek Harness that turns a rough id
ea draft into a polished, agent-ready prompt through iterative **rewrite → self-review → fix** round
draft into a polished, agent-ready prompt through iterative **rewrite → self-review → fix** rounds.
English | 简体中文
## Features
- One-click **Optimize** button on the input box plus domain recommendation chips; multi-round optim

ization with retry and per-round diff preview
- **Role library** (`<slug>.md` files): a 165-role cat
alog ships inside the package and is used whenever `rolesDir` is unset; list roles on demand, recomm

end by draft, re-run with an explicit role; set a default role in the settings page
- **Skill awaren
ess** (`skillAware`): when a draft matches an installed skill, its name and description are folded i
nto the meta-prompt so the output references those skills — guarded by exact-name constraints agains
t hallucination. Chinese and English drafts both match: a built-in bilingual gloss bridges Chinese t

erms like 页面／接口／部署 to English-described skills and back
- **Optimization directions**: five chips on
the preview panel (more concise / more detailed / more technical / restructure / stronger acceptanc
e) re-run the round toward a picked direction and echo the active one; directions are a fixed enum —

no free text, so no prompt injection
- **Prompt library**: save any result with one click; the libr
ary button on the input row opens a management panel — browse, expand, insert into the draft, re-opt

imize from a stored entry, or delete with a two-step confirm (newest first)
- **Output language foll
ows the agent UI language**: a Chinese interface yields Chinese prompts, English yields English, whi

le code identifiers, paths and commands stay verbatim
- Inline **Optimize** entry on queued (unsent)

conversation items
- **Acceptance criteria**: mechanical criteria ship with an executable check-com

items
- **Acceptance criteria**: mechanical criteria ship with an executable check-command template
## Judging an optimization
The result is more than the rewritten text — every block in the preview panel is review material:
| Panel block | What it is | How to judge with it |

| Optimized text | The rewritten prompt | Read it against the draft column, section by section |
| C
hanges | Each edit the model says it made | Ask per bullet: did it make the task clearer? Was anythi

ng changed that should not have been? |
| Acceptance criteria | Conditions that define done | Mechan
ical ones run via the check button; the rest verify by their stated judgment point — none verifiable

means suspicious |
| Skills | Installed skills matched this round | Skill mentions in the result mu

st use exact listed names; with none listed, the result must not invent any |
| Critique | Revision
log of the system-prompt second round | Does each revision say what changed and why? |
Quick checklist:

1. **Zero detail loss** — paths, versions, commands, and numbers preserved verbatim;
2. **Clear stru

cture** — goal, context, constraints, and expected output stated separately;
3. **No inventions** —

no facts the draft never stated (file names, error text, requirements);
4. **Verifiable acceptance**

— every criterion checkable by command or judgment point;
5. **Sound skill references** — named ski
lls genuinely fit the task and match their exact names.
When any check fails: hit **Regenerate** — the rejected result rides into the next round as a prior
attempt, so the model must produce a meaningfully different revision; or click a direction chip (mor
e concise / more detailed / more technical / restructure / stronger acceptance) to re-run toward tha
t direction; or re-run with another role, or switch to the system-prompt mode. Save what works with
**Save to prompt library**, then recall, re-optimize, or delete it any time from the library button
library**, then recall, re-optimize, or delete it any time from the library button on the input row.

| Package | npm | Purpose |
| `packages/prompt-optimizer` | @yimiliya/dsh-prompt-optimizer | Host service: optimization rounds,

role library, skill hints, model routing |
| `packages/api-prompt-optimizer` | @yimiliya/dsh-api-pro

mpt-optimizer | Remote controller and Typert descriptors (host/client shared method table) |

ages/client-ui-prompt-optimizer` | @yimiliya/dsh-client-ui-prompt-optimizer | Browser UI: trigger bu

tton, preview panel, queue entries, settings page |

izer-bundle | Profile bundle (`cordis.patch.yml`) that installs all three plugins in one shot |
Each package carries its own README, which npm renders on the package page; this document is the fam
ily-level view. `tools/tsdown.client.ts` is the standalone client build preset: it emits browser clo
sure artifacts against the harness `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({id, factory})` contract, with CSS
Modules compiled by lightningcss into self-contained injected styles.

## Privacy
Optimization runs are recorded in the session's own event log; treat drafts accordingly:
- Every optimization round appends a `plugin:prompt-optimizer/llm-request` record containing the ful

l draft text and the auxiliary system prompt.
- Every check run appends a `plugin:prompt-optimizer/v

erify` record containing the executed command and its (redacted) output.
- "Improve this role" rewri
tes the role definition file `<slug>.md` under the configured `rolesDir` on disk; the previous versi
on is kept alongside it as `<slug>.md.bak`. The bundled default catalog is read-only: configure `rol
esDir` to enable role evolution.
If you paste secrets into a draft, expect them to appear in the session log.
## Compatibility
The supported baseline is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` `0.2.1-rc.5`; earlier versions are unverified. Instal
led releases keep working across the whole `0.2.x` line via `engines.dsh` — details, including the q
ueue-entry slot requirement and the pinned peer dependencies, live in docs/compatibility.md, which i
s the single source of truth.
